notes:
PAGE INVENTORY
- https://en.unimib.it/study/bachelors-and-masters-degrees/economics-and-statistics-bachelors-degree-programmes — a category listing of several bachelor's degrees; it is the only supplied page that names "Economics and Science for Environmental Sustainability". It is not the programme's own page (no detail, no fees, no deadlines, no application channel), so programmePage = null.
- The other supplied pages are unrelated (institutional fees page, a PhD e-learning course page, a medicine internship e-learning course page, Erasmus pages, an e-learning search results page, international-admissions pages, equipollenza page). They contain no programme-specific facts for this bachelor's degree.

FACTS THAT COULD NOT BE EXTRACTED (no admissible quote)
- durationYears: no quote states 3 years / 6 semesters / 180 ECTS for this programme.
- tuition: no quote states ONE tuition amount in EUR for a non-EU student living abroad (or for international students in general) for this bachelor's degree for the current academic year. The only fees page is institutional ("Fees and funding" / "Contribution Guide for DEGREE COURSES - a.y. 2026/2027") and states no amount; Italian fees are ISEE-band based. Tuition left out on purpose.
- intakes: no quote states an application start/opening date or a dated deadline (day + month + year) and none states a recurring deadline (day + month) for this programme. The only dated statement found is for equipollenza appointments ("A partire dal 1° aprile fino al 28 maggio 2026"), which is not an application deadline for this programme, so it was not used. Intakes left out.
- applicationChannel: the international-admissions page says applications for bachelor's and master's degrees from holders of foreign qualifications go through the apply.unimib.it portal ("da oggi è possibile candidarsi ai corsi di Laurea e Laurea Magistrale UNIMIB tramite il portale apply.unimib.it"), but this is a general statement, not tied to this programme, and it does not name Universitaly for the application itself; the Universitaly mention on that page is only for the pre-enrolment receipt ("PER I CANDIDATI EXTRA-UE RICHIEDENTI VISTO: la ricevuta di pre-enrolment sul Portale UNIVERSITALY"), which is a visa step, not the application channel. Given the task's definition, no applicationChannel value could be produced with a quote that satisfies it for this programme, so the fact is left out; a human should verify the channel on the programme's own page.
- requirements language_proficiency (english): acceptedTests lists only the tests named in the quotes ('ielts', 'toefl'); the institution's page names many more English certificates (Cambridge FCE/CAE/CPE, TOEIC, PTE, Trinity ISE, LanguageCert, Oxford Test of English, etc.) which were not included to keep the list strictly to quoted names. Note the same page requires a B2 English certificate for non-EU visa-requesting candidates of English-taught programmes; the 5.5 IELTS quote is the numeric threshold given.
- documents: the international-admissions page lists many documents (secondary-school diploma, transcript, pre-enrolment receipt on UNIVERSITALY, B2 language certificate, CIMEA certificates, etc.), but these are stated for all bachelor's/master's applicants, not for this programme specifically; per the rules they were not listed as programme documents in the JSON. The language and prior-study-year rules above do explicitly apply to "corsi di laurea di primo livello (3 anni)" and are the closest admissible evidence for an international applicant.
